issues.t: Head gasket failure and overheating (Northstar head bolts)
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, the temperature gauge climbs on hills or under load, white exhaust smoke with a sweet smell, or pressure in the coolant tank that stays after the engine cools.
issues.why: The aluminum Northstar-family V8 is known for head bolt threads pulling out of the block, which lets the head gaskets leak. Owners report it most often from about 65,000 to 80,000 miles.
issues.next: If the gauge climbs, pull over and shut the engine off; driving an overheating aluminum engine can ruin it. Ask a shop for a combustion-gas test of the coolant. A proper repair usually means thread inserts or studs, not just new gaskets, so get a firm quote first. Avoid stop-leak products.

issues.t: Oil leak between the upper and lower crankcase halves
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, oil coating the bottom of the engine, or a burning-oil smell after driving.
issues.why: The 4.0L V8 is built with a split crankcase, and the sealant along that joint and the oil pan can let go with age. GM issued service bulletins on these leaks and on improved oil pan sealing.
issues.next: Check the oil level often so it never runs low. Have the leak traced and cleaned so a shop can see whether it is the crankcase joint, the oil pan or a head gasket. Small seeps can be watched; heavy leaks should be fixed.

issues.t: Stalls or won't restart from a failing crankshaft sensor
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or at a stop, sometimes won't restart for several minutes, then runs normally again. Power steering and brake assist get much heavier when the engine dies.
issues.why: A failing crankshaft position sensor stops the engine computer from knowing where the engine is, so it shuts off spark and fuel. RepairPal has dozens of Aurora reports, often past 100,000 miles. Some 2001 owners also needed an ignition switch.
issues.next: If it stalls, steer firmly to a safe spot and brake hard; the controls still work but take more effort. Have codes read soon, even if no warning light came on. Avoid highway driving until it is fixed.

issues.t: Fuel rail tubing can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A strong raw-gasoline smell around the engine, or wet spots on the engine near the fuel injectors.
issues.why: The nylon tubes in the original fuel rail can crack from heat, age and alcohol-blended fuel, letting fuel spray into the engine bay where it can catch fire. GM recall 04V-110 replaces the rail with a stainless steel one.
issues.next: If you smell fuel under the hood, don't drive it; have it towed. Ask an Oldsmobile-era GM dealer to check your VIN for recall 04V-110.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from the water pump cover or thermostat housing
issues.sym: Coolant smell, pink or orange crust around the front of the engine, and a coolant tank that needs topping off.
issues.why: GM bulletins for the 4.0L list coolant leaks from a loose water pump cover and thermostat housing. A cracked coolant tank, the water pump itself or the radiator neck can also leak.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up with the correct coolant and watch the gauge. Have a pressure test done to find the leak before it causes overheating.

issues.t: Overheating that is hard to trace
issues.sym: The temperature gauge runs hot, a hot-engine message appears, and the engine may shut itself off to protect itself.
issues.why: Owners report overheating that survives new radiators, thermostats and belts. On this engine, a hidden head gasket leak pushing exhaust into the coolant is a common cause that a basic pressure test can miss.
issues.next: Stop driving as soon as the gauge climbs. Ask a shop to test the coolant for combustion gases and to check the cooling fans and water pump, not just replace parts one by one.

issues.t: Knock or tick noise on a cold start
issues.sym: A knocking or ticking noise for a short time after a cold start that fades as the engine warms up.
issues.why: GM issued a 1999 service bulletin for a cold knock or tick on these engines. It is usually not harmful but should be checked if it lasts.
issues.next: Note how long it lasts and whether the oil level is correct. If the noise stays when warm or gets louder, have a shop listen to it.

issues.t: Delayed or harsh shift into reverse or drive
issues.sym: A pause and then a thump when shifting from park into reverse or drive, or harsh shifts when cold. Cruise control may also stop working.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover delayed or harsh garage shifts on these cars. In some cases a faulty engine computer causes harsh shifts and cruise problems, not the transmission itself.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and condition. Have codes read and ask about GM's bulletin before agreeing to a rebuild.

issues.t: Hard shifting that goes away after a restart
issues.sym: Hard or jerky shifts that clear up after the car sits turned off for a few minutes.
issues.why: Owners of the second-generation car report harsh shifts that a new transmission did not fix but a GM computer software update did.
issues.next: Have the transmission and engine computers checked for software updates and stored codes before replacing the transmission.

issues.t: Flickering lights and swinging charging voltage
issues.sym: Headlights and dash lights flicker or pulse, the voltage gauge swings, and in some cases the engine stalls.
issues.why: Owners describe charging voltage jumping between normal and too high, usually traced to the alternator and its built-in voltage regulator.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested. Too-high voltage can damage the battery and electronics, so don't put it off.

issues.t: Clunk or click in the steering when turning
issues.sym: A clunk, click or grinding feel through the steering wheel when turning slowly, often worse in the cold.
issues.why: The intermediate steering shaft between the column and the rack wears and binds. GM supplied a lube kit as a temporary fix, and replacement shafts were back-ordered for months.
issues.next: Have the steering shaft and tie rods inspected. If the steering ever feels stuck or loose, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Power steering rack leaks or fails
issues.sym: Hard steering at low speed, a power steering fluid leak, a whine, or in severe cases loss of steering control.
issues.why: Owners report failed racks, some replaced more than once, plus pump and hose failures. One reported a rack that fractured at high mileage.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level. If steering gets hard or erratic, stop driving and have the rack, hoses and pump inspected.

issues.t: ABS unit can leak internally (recall)
issues.sym: ABS, traction or stability warning lights, or ABS and stability control not working as they should.
issues.why: Some 2001 Auroras have an internal fluid leak in the ABS hydraulic unit, so rear brake balance, ABS and stability control may not work as designed. Recall 00V114000 has dealers inspect and replace the unit.
issues.next: Ask a GM dealer to check your VIN for recall 00V114000. Brake gently and leave extra distance until the brakes are checked.

issues.t: Airbag inflator can break apart (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: The airbag inflator could break apart when it fires, throwing fragments and leaving the bag under-inflated. GM recall 02V222000 covers it.
issues.next: Check your VIN with a GM dealer or at nhtsa.gov/recalls. The fix is free.

issues.t: Fuel can leak during refueling (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel dripping under the car after filling up.
issues.why: A fuel tank pressure sensor problem can let parts of the fuel system be damaged during refueling, which can cause leaks and a fire risk. GM recall 03V238000 covers it.
issues.next: If you smell fuel after filling up, park outdoors away from ignition sources and have it towed. Ask a GM dealer to check for recall 03V238000.

issues.t: Headlights work only some of the time
issues.sym: Headlights flicker, won't come on, or won't turn off as expected.
issues.why: RepairPal lists headlight operation problems as one of the most-reported Aurora issues, usually traced to the headlight switch.
issues.next: Don't drive at night until the headlights work reliably. Have a shop test the switch and wiring.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong or swings
issues.sym: The fuel gauge swings between full and empty, reads low with a full tank, or a low-fuel warning appears when it shouldn't.
issues.why: GM issued a 1998 bulletin for gauges that swing when the tank is full, and 2001 owners report erratic gauges. The sending unit in the tank or the cluster can be at fault.
issues.next: Use the trip odometer to track fuel until it is fixed so you don't run out. Have the sender and gauge tested.

issues.t: Gauges or tachometer act erratically
issues.sym: The tachometer jumps to high rpm, gauges or the odometer go dead, or the whole cluster cuts out and then resets.
issues.why: Owners report instrument cluster faults on the second-generation Aurora. Replacement clusters became hard to find, so repair is usually by a cluster rebuild service.
issues.next: Have codes read to rule out a charging or sensor problem first. A cluster rebuild is often an alternative to a new part.

issues.t: Keyless entry, trunk release and sunroof stop working
issues.sym: Several features stop at once, such as remote locks, trunk and fuel door release, sunroof and interior lights, even though fuses are good.
issues.why: On these cars the driver's master window switch passes power to several of those circuits, so a failed switch can knock them all out.
issues.next: Have the driver's window switch tested before replacing other modules. It is usually a simple part to swap.

issues.t: Shake or vibration at highway speed
issues.sym: Steering wheel, seat or floor vibration at highway speeds on smooth roads.
issues.why: GM issued service bulletins for highway-speed vibration on these cars, usually fixed by careful wheel and tire balancing or tire matching.
issues.next: Have the tires road-force balanced and inspected for damage. If shaking starts suddenly, check for a loose wheel or damaged tire right away.

issues.t: Front-end clunk or rattle over bumps
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle from the front of the car over bumps or rough pavement.
issues.why: GM issued a 1999 bulletin for front-end clunks on this car. Worn links, mounts or struts are typical causes.
issues.next: Have the front suspension and steering parts inspected for wear or looseness.

issues.t: Rusted floor under the battery compartment
issues.sym: Rust holes in the floor near the battery, water getting in, or a battery that sits crooked or loose.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for floor pan corrosion and holes in the battery compartment area.
issues.next: Have the battery tray and floor inspected, especially if you smell battery acid or see water inside. Rust repair is easier while it is small.

issues.t: Heated seat stops warming
issues.sym: One or both heated front seats stop getting warm.
issues.why: GM issued a 1999 bulletin for failed seat heater elements on these cars.
issues.next: Have the seat heater circuit tested. The heating pad in the seat is usually the part that fails.

issues.t: Headliner sags near the sunroof
issues.sym: The roof lining droops near the sunroof opening.
issues.why: A GM bulletin covers headliner sag at the sunroof on these cars, caused by the backing and adhesive loosening with age and heat.
issues.next: This is cosmetic. An upholstery shop can re-glue or replace the headliner.

issues.t: Paint cracking and peeling
issues.sym: Paint cracking, flaking or peeling, often on the roof, hood and trunk.
issues.why: Owners of 1998 Auroras report the clear coat and paint failing after years of sun exposure.
issues.next: This is cosmetic, but bare metal can rust. Touch up or repaint exposed areas.
